name: vpcs
desc: Virtual PC simulator for testing IP routing
why: A virtual PC simulator for IP routing, a small window into how routing and ARP-style behaviour actually work.

brief.what_it_is: VPCS is a small virtual PC simulator, a command-line program written in C that runs on Linux, Cygwin, or BSD. According to its SourceForge page, it can simulate up to 9 PCs, and you can ping and traceroute them, or ping and traceroute other hosts and routers from them. It is described as just a program running on Linux or Windows, with only a few network commands available. The pages I read do not describe its input format or command syntax, so I can only say what it does, not how you drive it.
brief.why_it_exists: The page frames it as a lightweight stand-in for full PCs when studying Cisco routers in Dynamips: it can replace the routers or VMware boxes that would otherwise be used as PCs in a Dynamips network.
brief.install_notes: The SourceForge page lists Linux as the platform badge, with Cygwin and BSD under operating systems. It is licensed under the BSD License. I did not find install steps, build instructions, or first-run configuration on the pages I read. A reviewer on the page reports difficulty downloading, and one points to use with GNS3.
brief.standout: It is a tiny, single-purpose PC that stands in for a full VM or a router-as-PC inside a Dynamips/GNS3 lab, so you can ping and traceroute from it without booting anything heavy. A reviewer says it can send UDP and TCP pings, which is useful for testing ACLs.
brief.status: quiet. The SourceForge page shows Last Update 2016-11-15, Registered 2011-12-02, 26 downloads this week, and 3 reviews with a 4.0 average (newest review 2014-10-02). I found no newer release or commit in what I fetched, so this is an inference from dates, not a confirmed abandonment.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a SourceForge project page, not a README, and it is cluttered with unrelated ads and listings. I found no command examples, no docs, and no wiki content in either fetch, so the commands_seen list is empty. The platform listing is inconsistent: the badge shows Linux, the details list BSD, Cygwin, and Linux, and the description mentions Windows. The project's last recorded update is from 2016, so it may not track current systems.
quotes: The VPCS can simulate up to 9 PCs.
VPCS is not the traditional PC, it is just a program running on the Linux or Windows, and only few network commands can be used in it.
VPCS can replace the routers or VMware boxes which are used as PCs in the Dynamips network.
